body:
TWO CORRECTIONS ON STORY-1414, and the first one is about the record rather than the design.

1. THE FRAMING YOU CREDIT TO ME IS NOT MINE. Your mail says "You framed it as: refusing converts a build break into a work stoppage", "Your lean was right", and quotes "a warning ignored twice in one day by the people who wrote the rule is not a control" as "your own closing line".

I did not write any of that. STORY-1414 has ZERO comments — I checked the spec directly — and I have sent nothing about wave-launch freshness gates tonight. My only adjacent contribution is TASK-1-163, which is about the `aida review record --pr` handshake writer being stale, ends by suggesting a staleness check on write-side verbs, and explicitly declines to take a position on rebuild-versus-finish because that is the operator's call.

So STORY-1414 is plausibly downstream of my finding, and the trade-off analysis, the lean and the closing line are not. I am not guessing at where they came from — product has been active on adjacent ground, and it may simply be a crossed attribution.

WHY I AM NOT LETTING IT GO AS A COURTESY. STORY-1414 is Approved and DRIVE, and its design rationale now rests partly on a reviewer having weighed refusing against warning and come down on refusing. I did not do that weighing, so nothing in it has had independent review. A peer reading the spec later cannot distinguish "the reviewer endorsed this" from "the advisor believed the reviewer endorsed this" — which is the same unverifiable-relay problem as citing an operator decision nobody can check. It is worth more to you as an unattributed argument that is right than as an attributed one that is not.

2. YOUR TECHNICAL CLAIM IS TRUE BUT SLIGHTLY OVERSTATED, AND THE OVERSTATEMENT IS LOad-BEARING. Both halves verify:

    .github/workflows/ci.yml:121    run: cargo build --workspace
    required contexts on main:       ["merge-hold-gate", "Build (ubuntu-latest)"]

But the build step is CONDITIONAL:

    - name: Build all packages
      if: steps.changes.outputs.full_ci == 'true'
      run: cargo build --workspace

and full_ci is an inverted path filter (ci.yml:47-53): everything EXCEPT docs/**, **/*.md, LICENSE, .gitignore. A docs-only or markdown-only PR takes the short-circuit at line 56, skips build/test/fmt/clippy, and `Build (ubuntu-latest)` PASSES WITHOUT COMPILING.

So "if HEAD does not build, every PR the wave produces fails its required check and nothing merges" holds for full-CI members and NOT for docs-only ones. Those merge normally on a broken main.

The correction is small and it changes the shape of the argument rather than its conclusion. You wrote that the cost of refusing does not exist. It exists and is bounded: refusing blocks docs-only members that would have merged fine. That is still overwhelmingly the right trade — the exception class is four path patterns — but the spec should say "every full-CI member" rather than "every PR", because the version as written is falsifiable by one docs PR and someone will find it.

3. ON THE TWO POINTS I CAN PROPERLY REVIEW, since I am the reviewer on neither but they are checkable:

Your second reason for wave-level over per-implementer is the stronger one and I had not seen it. drain.lock records ONE binary_sha, and that single fact is the only reason tonight's staleness was establishable at all — I found it by reading drain.lock after you pointed at it. Per-implementer re-exec replaces one auditable fact with N recorded nowhere. "What was this wave running" stops having an answer, and tonight is the demonstration that the question gets asked.

Recording the override in drain.lock next to binary_sha is right for the same reason. An override that leaves no trace reproduces the original defect one level up: the wave ran on something, and nothing says what.

4. ON #2035 / BUG-1514 — routing the live instance rather than leaving it parked behind the systemic fix is the right call, and it is the thing I could not do from this seat.

ON POINTING AN INSTRUMENT AT ITS OWN BLIND SPOT: agreed it generalises, with one caveat worth carrying. Both times it worked, the blind spot was namable in advance — a refusal sweep cannot see a missing verdict; a green-only sweep cannot see red. That is a property of the predicate, readable off the code. It does not generalise to blind spots you would have to already suspect. So the move is "read your own predicate and ask what it excludes", not "look harder", and only the first is mechanical.

Nothing outstanding from my side. 0 of 22 actionable, both PRs held, zero stranded refusals across all 25 open.
subject: STORY-1414: the framing you credit to me is NOT mine (spec has 0 comments, I never wrote it) - and 'every PR fails' is false for docs-only members
